// --- Decision log ---
// 2026-08-27 v2 draft (external feedback pass — more lands, faster mana, Urza package;
// full rationale + card-by-card evaluation of both example decks in deck/ulalek-v2-proposal.md):
//   OUT -> IN, 10 swaps:
//     Snow-Covered Wastes   -> Planar Nexus         (every nonbasic land type: single-handedly
//                                                    "powers" any Urza land; Locus; {1}: any color)
//     Cascading Cataracts   -> Urza's Tower          }  Urza package: any one Urza land + Nexus
//     Shivan Reef           -> Urza's Mine           }  is 4-5 mana from 2 lands; all fetchable
//     Awakening Zone        -> Urza's Power Plant    }  via Crop Rotation/Sylvan Scrying/Mycospawn
//     Eldrazi Conscription  -> Reflecting Pool      (2nd Command Tower; copies Tomb/Temple "2" too)
//     Summon: Bahamut       -> Boseiju, Who Endures (interaction in a land slot)
//     Eldrazi Displacer     -> Roaming Throne       (names Eldrazi; DOUBLES ULALEK'S OWN TRIGGER =
//                                                    two {C}{C} copy-everything rounds per cast;
//                                                    also doubles annihilator/ETB/LTB/Azlask.
//                                                    NOTE: does NOT double "when you cast" triggers
//                                                    of spells on the stack (CR 109.2, "creature you
//                                                    control" = permanent) — that's Echoes' job)
//     Emergence Zone        -> Liberator, Urza's Battlethopter (same job, repeatable: flash for
//                                                    ~the whole deck; deploy on end steps to dodge
//                                                    sorcery wipes — upgrades the 2026-08-26
//                                                    resilience plan; Winding Canyons stays as the
//                                                    creature-flash backup)
//     Worn Powerstone       -> Thran Dynamo         (feedback: more/denser ramp)
//     Nulldrifter           -> Mystic Forge         (Forge is in BOTH example decks; ~80% of deck
//                                                    castable off the top = Nulldrifter's card-
//                                                    advantage job, every turn; Nulldrifter was the
//                                                    weakest cast trigger in the crowded 7+ slot.
//                                                    Alternate cut if no big should go: Abstruse
//                                                    Archaic)
//   2026-08-27 owner rulings (recorded, don't re-litigate): KEEP Herald of Kozilek, KEEP
//   Hideous Taskmaster, KEEP Path of Annihilation; Devourer of Destiny REJECTED.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up (owner): Forest -> Emergence Zone (Zone back in as wipe insurance /
//   Liberator backup; also flashes NONcreature spells, e.g. EOT All Is Dust). Cost accepted:
//   Nature's Lore/Three Visits down to 3 targets (Breeding Pool/Stomping Ground/Ketria — they
//   fetch untapped and preferred those anyway; Boseiju is NOT a Forest card), Prismatic Vista
//   down to 2 basics (Island/Mountain). Lands stay 36.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 2 (owner): Prismatic Vista -> Vesuva. Audit confirmed Vista was the
//   ONLY basic-only fetcher (Lore/Visits = Forest CARD incl. duals; Misty/Scalding/Foothills =
//   typed; Crop/Scrying/Mycospawn = any land), and with 2 basic targets it was the weakest
//   land in the list. Vesuva: enters tapped, but = Temple/Tomb #2 or Tower #2 (Tower +
//   Vesuva-Tower + Nexus = 7 mana from 3 lands), or copy the table's best land.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 3 (owner): APPLIED Island -> Tropical Island, Mountain -> Volcanic
//   Island (nothing basic-only remains, so duals are strictly better fixing for the same
//   fetches; Volcanic serves the kept Herald {1}{U}{R} and Mana Drain {U}{U}; Tropical is a
//   Lore/Visits target). Owner rationale for accepting ZERO basics: deck was ~94% nonbasic
//   anyway, and mass land denial is forbidden at bracket 3. Residual edge case: Blood
//   Moon-style replacement effects (not MLD by WotC's definition) and opponents'
//   Field of Ruin/Ghost Quarter — revisit basics only if those appear in the pod.
//   Proxy note: Tropical/Volcanic are >=25EUR -> proxy candidates for the buylist.
//   Sim (20k games/side, same script both sides): 7 mana by T5 51%->53%, by T6 68%->71%;
//   commander by T4 63%->65%. Urza pair "powered" by T6 in ~18% of games (upside wedge, not
//   engine). Haymaker-in-hand by T6 dips 48%->40% from losing 3 of 12 MV7+ pieces
//   (Conscription, Bahamut, Nulldrifter) — Forge/Sanctum/Conduit offset this but aren't modeled.
//   Combos re-verified (Commander Spellbook): still exactly the two allowed late-game lines
//   (Basalt+Forsaken Monument; Ulalek+Echoes+Unsealing). No new Game Changers — still at cap 3
//   (Mana Vault, Ancient Tomb, Crop Rotation); Boseiju confirmed NOT a GC (Aug-2026 list).
//   Feedback's "Basalt + Eldrazi Monument" concern = Basalt + FORSAKEN Monument, already
//   adjudicated 2026-08-19 as a deliberate late-game keep (rule-0 it at the table).
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 4 (owner: "Great Henge has poor synergy"). Confirmed by data — Henge
//   is the LOWEST-signal card in the list: 6% EDHREC inclusion for Ulalek, synergy +0.003
//   (statistical noise). Mechanically it is win-more here: cost reduction keys off greatest
//   power among creatures you control, so it is cheap only once a fatty already resolved, and
//   {G}{G} in a 94%-nonbasic 5-color-identity shell is the deck's hardest color requirement.
//   Two swaps, both aimed at the weakest side of the deck (see below):
//     The Great Henge  -> Garruk's Uprising   ({2}{G}, 53% inclusion, synergy +0.40)
//        - Fixed 3 mana on T3 vs Henge's 2-to-9 chicken-and-egg; one G, not GG.
//        - 15 of 25 creatures are power 4+, INCLUDING every single MV7+ haymaker — so it
//          converts "I finally cast my bomb" into "bomb + a card", and the Ulalek/Echoes copy
//          of a creature spell makes a TOKEN copy that also enters and draws again.
//        - Second mode is the real prize: TEAM-WIDE trample. Audit found only 4 creatures
//          with native trample and no team-wide source at all, while the deck runs 4
//          annihilator bodies (Azlask, Flayer, Taskmaster, Ulamog the Defiler) that get
//          chump-blocked all day. Trample is what turns the Azlask/Path of Annihilation
//          overrun plan into actual lethal. (Wording correction to the first draft of this
//          note: Eldrazi Conscription also grants trample, but only to ONE enchanted
//          creature — it was never the team-wide source, so the two do not overlap.)
//        - Caveat: Uprising is GREEN, so Echoes of Eternity (colorless-only) does NOT double
//          its trigger. Henge wasn't doubled either. No loss.
//     Sylvan Scrying   -> Ancient Stirrings   ({G}, 35% inclusion, synergy +0.33)
//        - Measured the deck: 88 of 99 cards are COLORLESS cards (88.9%). Only 11 misses
//          (Beast Within, Crop Rotation, Heroic Intervention, Imprisoned in the Moon, Mana
//          Drain, Nature's Lore, Stubborn Denial, Shadow in the Warp, Three Visits + the two
//          cards being cut). Odds all five cards off the top are colored = 462/C(99,5), i.e.
//          ~0.0006% — Stirrings is effectively "{G}: Impulse 5, take the best card."
//        - Strict rate upgrade over Scrying, which is a 2-mana sorcery that draws A LAND.
//          Stirrings costs 1, is a T1 play, and grabs a land when land-light OR a rock/threat
//          when land-heavy — which is exactly the flood insurance a 36-land deck wants.
//        - ACCEPTED COST (flagged, revert this line only if it bites): Scrying was 1 of 3
//          ways to fetch a SPECIFIC land, so the Urza's Mine/Power Plant/Tower assembly drops
//          to Crop Rotation + Sowing Mycospawn as guaranteed tutors. The v2 sim already rated
//          the Urza pair "an upside wedge, not an engine" (powered by T6 in ~18% of games),
//          and Stirrings still finds Urza pieces opportunistically since lands are colorless
//          cards. Owner's own standing rule — Tron-style synergy lands are low-value in
//          singleton — points the same way.
//   WEAKEST SIDE OF THE DECK (the finding behind both swaps): early/mid-game card FLOW and
//   post-wipe refuel. Every meaningful card-advantage piece is back-loaded onto already
//   casting a fatty — Kozilek's Unsealing draws 3 but ONLY on CREATURE spells MV7+ (verified
//   oracle; it does not see noncreature spells at all), Kozilek the Great Distortion refills
//   on ETB, the Ugins are 7-8 mana, Bonders' Enclave needs a power-4 body. Nothing at all
//   draws a card while you are ramping on T1-T5. With 36 lands + 16 ramp = 52 mana sources,
//   the deck's real failure mode is drawing the mana half, converting it to nothing, and
//   having no way to dig. Both new cards attack that window (1 mana and 3 mana) instead of
//   adding more top-end. Section counts unchanged: Draw & Engines stays 10, deck stays 99.
//   RISE OF THE ELDRAZI — re-evaluated on request, verdict still NO (but the 2026-08-26
//   reasoning was partly wrong, so recording the corrected version):
//     Oracle: {9}{C}{C}{C} Sorcery. Can't be countered. Destroy target permanent, target
//     player draws four cards, take an extra turn, then exile it.
//     - CORRECTION: it IS colorless, so Echoes of Eternity DOES copy it -> 2 extra turns,
//       2 permanents destroyed, draw 8. The old note underrated it there.
//     - But it is NOT an Eldrazi (plain Sorcery), so Ulalek never triggers off it, and it is
//       NOT a creature spell, so Kozilek's Unsealing does NOT draw 3, Eye of Ugin and Eldrazi
//       Temple do NOT reduce it, and Conduit of Ruin cannot tutor it.
//     - So it is a 12-mana card that misses every engine in the deck and only shines off a
//       6-mana enchantment that is already the best card here. At 12 mana we would rather
//       untap with Emrakul or Ulamog, which win the game outright. Worse, it adds top-end to
//       a deck whose diagnosed weakness is the MIDDLE. Deferred again — and it is a 21EUR
//       card doing a worse job than a 0.29EUR one.
//   Verification: Commander Spellbook re-run on the exact post-swap 99 — still EXACTLY the
//   two allowed late-game lines (Basalt + Forsaken Monument; Ulalek + Echoes + Unsealing),
//   no new lines from either addition. Neither Garruk's Uprising nor Ancient Stirrings is on
//   the Aug-2026 Game Changer list, so GC count stays at the bracket-3 cap of 3 (Mana Vault,
//   Ancient Tomb, Crop Rotation). Buylist delta: OUT Great Henge + Sylvan Scrying, IN Garruk's
//   Uprising (0.57EUR) + Ancient Stirrings (0.29EUR) — both well under the 25EUR proxy line.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 5 (owner: Conscription cut in v2 was a miss, restore it).
//   REVERSED the v2 "Eldrazi Conscription -> Reflecting Pool" swap on the Conscription side.
//     Reality Smasher -> Eldrazi Conscription
//   Why Conscription belongs (owner is right, and the v2 pass undervalued it):
//     - Oracle {8}, "Kindred Enchantment — ELDRAZI Aura" — it IS an Eldrazi spell, so casting
//       it triggers Ulalek. Pay {C}{C} -> copy all spells you control -> a second Conscription.
//       It is also COLORLESS, so Echoes of Eternity copies it independently. Ulalek is a 2/5;
//       two Conscriptions make it a 22/25 with TRAMPLE and annihilator 4. That is a one-shot
//       kill plus a 4-permanent strip, and it is a documented win package in ulalek-b3-playbook.md.
//     - EDHREC 47% inclusion / +0.44 synergy — higher synergy than anything added in v2.
//     - Restores the MV7+ haymaker count the v2 sim flagged as dropping (48%->40% in hand by T6).
//   THE CUT IS SKITTERING CICADA. (First attempt cut Fellwar Stone on a pure card-quality
//   argument — Fellwar makes "any COLOR an opponent's land could produce" and colorless is not
//   a color, so it is the one rock that cannot pay {C}, which is what Ulalek's {C}{C} copy tax,
//   Kozilek's Command {X}{C}{C}, Echoes {3}{C}{C}{C} and Kozilek the Great Distortion {8}{C}{C}
//   demand. True, but the SIM said cutting any mana source is the wrong trade — see below.
//   Fellwar Stone stays; revisit it only if the deck ever wants a 100th slot.)
//   Cut-candidate sim, 20k games each, one script, each row = add Conscription and cut that card,
//   measured as delta vs the pre-swap v2 list:
//       CUT                          cmd by T4   7 mana by T6   MV7+ by T7
//       Fellwar Stone                   -3.1        -2.4          +0.8
//       Mind Stone                      -2.9        -1.8          +0.3
//       Arcane Signet                   -2.8        -1.7          +0.3
//       Reflecting Pool (land 36->35)   -0.6        -0.7          +0.2
//       Skittering Cicada / Thief /
//         Abstruse Archaic (non-mana)   -0.1        -0.2          +2.5
//     Reading: cutting ANY mana source costs ~3 points of commander-on-T4 and buys nothing,
//     because Conscription is an 8-drop Aura that needs the mana AND a body. Cutting a cheap
//     NON-mana spell is nearly free on speed and is the only option that actually raises
//     haymaker access (+2.5 by T7), since it trades a 3-drop for a 12th MV7+ payoff.
//     (Absolute values in this script are not comparable to the numbers logged earlier in this
//     file — different script. Only the deltas within this table are valid, per CLAUDE.md.)
//   THE CUT IS REALITY SMASHER (owner-proposed, and it is the best of the candidates).
//     - Oracle: {4}{C} 5/5 Eldrazi, trample + haste, "Whenever this creature becomes the target
//       of a spell an opponent controls, counter that spell unless its controller discards a
//       card." Owner's read is exactly right on all three counts: the rider only sees TARGETED
//       opposing spells, so it does nothing against sweepers (Wrath/Damnation/Blasphemous Act
//       and our own All Is Dust do not target), nothing against edicts, and the "tax" is one
//       discard — late game an opponent pitches a dead land and moves on. It is a speed bump,
//       not protection, and nobody spends targeted removal on a 5/5 in a deck full of Ulamogs.
//     - EDHREC: does not even REGISTER for Ulalek (below the reporting threshold; general rank
//       10563). Compare Thief of Existence at 16% and Abstruse Archaic's unique effect. It is
//       the only creature in the list with no measurable presence in the archetype.
//     - What we lose is real but small: it is an MV5 Eldrazi, so it triggered Ulalek, took the
//       Temple/Eye/Incubator discounts, made 2 Spawn off Kozilek's Unsealing, drew off Garruk's
//       Uprising, and a Ulalek copy gave a second hasty 5/5 trampler. But it is a plain beater
//       in a deck whose payoffs are annihilator, board theft and exile, and 9 other Eldrazi at
//       MV<=5 still fill the early-Ulalek-trigger role.
//     - Sim (60k games/side, 3 seeds): cutting it is FREE — cmd by T4 +0.1, 7 mana by T6 -0.1,
//       MV7+ by T6 +2.2, MV7+ by T7 +2.5. Identical to cutting Thief or Archaic, and strictly
//       better than cutting a land (Tomb of the Spirit Dragon: -0.9 / -1.5).
//   SUPERSEDED CUT CANDIDATES (recorded so they are not re-proposed):
//   (SUPERSEDED, recorded so it is not re-proposed: this slot first cut Skittering Cicada on a
//   "strictly dominated by Liberator" argument. Owner overruled, correctly — the claim was
//   wrong on two counts. (1) Liberator dominates only the FLASH clause; Cicada's second ability
//   is a different card entirely — +X/+X where X is the cast spell's mana value, and it STACKS
//   across multiple casts in a turn, which this deck does routinely off its cost reducers. Cast
//   a 7-drop and a 5-drop precombat and Cicada swings as a 14/14. (2) The trample was called
//   redundant with Garruk's Uprising — true for the trample keyword alone, but Uprising does not
//   PUMP, so the damage half is not duplicated. Two flash enablers is also a package, not waste:
//   the whole point of the 2026-08-26 resilience plan is reliably having one. Cicada STAYS.
//   Rules caveat on the pressure plan, for the playbook: Ulalek's and Echoes' copies are put on
//   the stack, NOT cast, so they do not trigger Cicada's "whenever you cast" pump. Only real
//   casts grow it.)
//   ABSTRUSE ARCHAIC was proposed as the cut and WITHDRAWN. It STAYS. The redundancy argument
//   (that Echoes of Eternity and Roaming Throne already double Ulalek's trigger for free) was
//   too strong: neither of those can copy an ACTIVATED ability, and Roaming Throne only sees
//   triggers of creatures — Archaic is the only piece that can copy Eye of Ugin's activation,
//   Mystic Forge, or a land ability. On Ulalek specifically it is a real engine:
//     - "{1}, {T}: Copy target activated or triggered ability you control from a colorless
//       source." Ulalek has devoid, so it IS a colorless source and its trigger is a legal target.
//     - COST CORRECTION for the playbook — it is NOT "a Ulalek copy for {1}". The WotC ruling on
//       Archaic states: "If a triggered ability asks you to pay a cost, you pay that cost for the
//       copy separately." Ulalek's trigger reads "you may pay {C}{C}", so the true price is {1}
//       + tap + {C}{C} = 3 mana for the second round of "copy all spells you control, then copy
//       all other activated and triggered abilities you control".
//     - It snowballs: Ulalek's trigger sits ABOVE the Eldrazi spell that caused it, so the spell
//       is still on the stack to be copied, and the copies made by the first resolution are
//       themselves spells on the stack when the original trigger resolves.
//   RULES NOTE for ulalek-b3-playbook.md (from the Ulalek rulings): "The copies are created on
//   the stack, so they're not cast... Abilities of copied spells that say 'When you cast [this
//   spell]' won't trigger." Two consequences: (1) Ulalek/Echoes copies do NOT grow Skittering
//   Cicada — only real casts do; (2) Thief of Existence's second exile comes from Ulalek copying
//   its TRIGGER on the stack, not from the token copy having a cast trigger.
//   Lands stay 36, Ramp stays 16. Ramp/Creatures/Threats counts: 16 / 21 / 4.
//   CORRECTION to the v2 log line "Reflecting Pool (2nd Command Tower; copies Tomb/Temple '2'
//   too)": half wrong. Reflecting Pool reads "Add one mana of any TYPE that a land you control
//   could produce" — type includes colorless, so it CAN make {C} (this is why it survives the
//   cut and Fellwar does not). But it produces ONE mana, so it does NOT copy Ancient Tomb's or
//   Eldrazi Temple's "{C}{C}". Only Vesuva actually copies those. Reflecting Pool stays.
//   Section counts: Creatures 22->21, Big Threats & Protection 3->4. Deck still 99.
//   Bracket unchanged: Conscription is not a Game Changer, GC count stays at the cap of 3.
//   Spellbook re-run on the exact post-restore 99: still EXACTLY the two allowed late-game
//   lines. Conscription's only near-line needs Rafiq of the Many, which is not in the deck.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 6 (owner: Volcanic Island is too expensive to actually play, even as
//   the flagged proxy candidate — price-driven exception to the "price never decides" rule,
//   explicitly owner-ruled for this slot).
//     Volcanic Island -> Sulfur Falls
//   Premise correction recorded during the decision: the deck's fetches and land tutors
//   (Misty/Scalding/Foothills, Crop Rotation, Sowing Mycospawn, Nature's Lore, Three Visits)
//   put lands onto the battlefield UNTAPPED unless the land's own text says otherwise — a
//   fetched Volcanic entered untapped. Molten Tributary (true Island Mountain, 0.22EUR) was
//   considered for keeping fetchability and REJECTED: it enters tapped every time, fetched or
//   drawn, and the fetchable-U/R niche is already covered (Scalding -> Steam Vents, Misty ->
//   Tropical, Foothills -> Stomping Ground). Sulfur Falls (0.29EUR) has NO basic land types
//   (checks "you control an Island or a Mountain" only), so it is invisible to all three
//   fetches — accepted; in exchange it enters untapped from T2 on in ~all games (Tropical,
//   Steam Vents, Breeding Pool and Ketria all carry the checked types; T1 it is always
//   tapped). U/R duty unchanged: Herald {1}{U}{R}, Mana Drain {U}{U}. Lands stay 36; no
//   GC/combo implications (checked: Sulfur Falls is not a Game Changer, adds no combo line).
//   Buylist delta: Volcanic Island (proxy candidate) out entirely, IN Sulfur Falls 0.29EUR.
//   2026-08-27 follow-up 7 (owner: same price call as follow-up 6, for the other dual).
//     Tropical Island -> Hinterland Harbor
//   Same colors (G/U), same check-land template as Sulfur Falls, 0.33EUR. Knock-on effects
//   accepted and recorded:
//     - Nature's Lore / Three Visits back down to 3 Forest-card targets (Breeding Pool,
//       Stomping Ground, Ketria Triome) — where they were before the follow-up 3 promotion.
//     - Harbor has no basic land types -> invisible to Misty/Scalding/Foothills; each fetch
//       still has 3-4 live targets (the shocks + Ketria).
//     - Sulfur Falls' untap check loses one Island; both check lands now lean on Steam Vents /
//       Breeding Pool / Ketria / Stomping Ground — and Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth auto-passes
//       Harbor's check (every land on the battlefield is a Forest with it out). Both are
//       always tapped on T1.
//   With this swap NOTHING >=25EUR remains in the land base; the reserved-list duals are gone
//   entirely rather than proxied. Lands stay 36, deck 99; no GC/combo implications.
//   Buylist delta: Tropical Island (proxy candidate) out entirely, IN Hinterland Harbor 0.33EUR.
// 2026-08-31 land-tutor pass (owner: Azlask feels weak here — tokens are mana, not an army;
//   wanted another land fetch to complete the Urza package / find Eye of Ugin). Two-for-two:
//     Tomb of the Spirit Dragon -> Urza's Cave      (land for land, lands stay 36)
//     Azlask, the Swelling Scourge -> Matter Reshaper (creature for creature, stays 21)
//   Why Azlask goes: his activation costs {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — five DIFFERENT colored pips at once.
//   All-color sources are only City of Brass/Mana Confluence/Command Tower/Planar Nexus/Path of
//   Ancestry (+ conditional Orchard/Reflecting Pool); holding all five colors simultaneously
//   essentially never happens, so the pump/annihilator mode is blank text and he is a 3-mana 2/2
//   collecting experience counters with no payoff.
//   LOG CORRECTION: the follow-up 4 note counted Azlask among "4 annihilator bodies" — wrong.
//   His annihilator grant is part of the uncastable WUBRG activation (and only hits Spawns/
//   Scions); he never contributed to that plan. Annihilator bodies are 3: Flayer, Taskmaster,
//   Ulamog the Defiler (+ Conscription's enchanted creature).
//   Why Urza's Cave: {3},{T},sac: any land onto the battlefield TAPPED, instant speed. Fetches
//   the missing Urza's Mine/Power-Plant/Tower piece, Planar Nexus, Eye of Ugin, Sanctum, Vesuva,
//   or EOT Winding Canyons/Emergence Zone. Restores a third guaranteed specific-land tutor —
//   exactly the flagged cost of the Sylvan Scrying -> Ancient Stirrings swap ("revert if it
//   bites") — without giving Stirrings back, and in a LAND slot ({C} until needed).
//   TYPE NOTE: its land type is "Urza's Cave", NOT Mine/Power-Plant/Tower — it FETCHES Tron
//   pieces but never powers them (that's Planar Nexus's job).
//   Expedition Map considered and REJECTED for the same job: eats a spell slot, dies to the
//   artifact hate already aimed at our 8+ rocks, and puts the land to HAND (competes with the
//   land drop). Map's only edges: 3 total mana vs 4, T1 deploy, fetched land can be played
//   untapped (mostly relevant for Ancient Tomb). Cave's slot economics win.
